text:
anna: FYI I just noticed a 20-30% tail latency regression on our INT8 inference profile after the last quantization merge (#4321).
raj: ugh. which fleet / model? can you repro locally?
anna: repros on stage (g5.2xlarge) with the bert-ish serving profile. CI perf test also failed on the nightly run — ci-bot posted it at 04:12 UTC.
ci-bot: nightly-perf-test failed: latency_p99 increased from 310ms -> 420ms on quant-int8 suite. see /ci/artifacts/2024-06-31/17199
marco: any obvious change in batching or kernel selection in the merge?
anna: merge touched dequant path in runtime/quantizer and introduced a new copying step before KV cache lookup. suspect dequant -> reorder -> re-quant overhead.
liz: can you paste the perf profile (nvprof / CUPTI) output? even a small flame graph helps.
anna: here are the quick profiling snippets from a 1k request run on stage:
```
GPU time (median): 120ms
GPU time (p99): 410ms
Dequant kernel: 35ms median (p99 220ms)
KV cache lookup + copy: 18ms median (p99 85ms)
Attention compute kernel: 45ms median
Batching idle: 2ms
```
looks like dequant is spiking.
raj: hmm, dequant kernel shouldn't be that big. did we switch from fused dequant+transpose to separate ops somewhere? that would add memory traffic.
anna: the merge replaced fused path with a more "portable" sequence for FP8 support. it added a temporary buffer and an explicit transpose before writing into KV cache.
marco: that explains extra memcpy. For small sequence lengths the memcopy overhead dominates.
liz: CI regression also triggered the rollout-blocker label on the release PR. we need a bisect and either revert or targeted fix before we promote.
anna: ran a quick git bisect locally, pinpointed commit 7f9b3a2 as the culprit (the refactor of quant kernels). will open a minimal revert PR unless someone has a cheaper fix.
raj: before revert, can we try toggling use_fused_dequant flag at runtime to see perf delta? probably fastest to test.
anna: toggled flag on stage: p99 dropped back to ~320ms within 10 minutes. pushing a hotfix to re-enable fused path for INT8 only.
deploy-bot: hotfix deploy started: canary -> 3 nodes. ETA 8m.
marco: also add a micro-benchmark in CI that runs the dequant kernel standalone with small seq lenses. running synthetic test will catch future regressions.
liz: agreed. add it under infra/perf/quant_kernels and mark as non-flaky. i'll create a ticket for adding a perf gate then.
anna: created revert PR: #4389 with description and perf numbers. also added a reproducer and the nvprof snippet.
raj: thanks. action items: 1) land revert/hotfix, 2) add micro-benchmark CI test, 3) plan follow-up to reintroduce FP8 portability without extra memcpy (kernel fusion work), 4) check KV cache write path for unnecessary copies.
liz: rolling this to oncall and ops: ping @ops for any capacity impact during revert canary.
anna: ops: canary stayed healthy during rollback, no errors observed. latency back to baseline on canary nodes.
ci-bot: nightly perf rerun (post-hotfix): all perf suites green.
```
quant-int8: latency_p99 315ms (baseline 310ms)
quant-fp16: ok
```
marco: closing rollback, but keep the revert PR open as a reminder until we implement fused-kernel approach.
liz: thanks everyone. feel free to DM if you want more traces. :thumbsup:
